title: Type-A Soergel Bimodules and Hecke Categorification

items.title: type a reflection realization and polynomial ring
items.statement: For n≥2 over k=Q, let R=Q[x_1,…,x_n] with deg(x_i)=2 and S_n act by place permutations. The coordinate roots β_i=x_i−x_{i+1} govern length; the alternating-sign roots α_i=ε_iβ_i (ε_iε_{i+1}=−1) give the balanced diagrammatic realization. It is faithful, reflection faithful, Demazure-surjective, balanced, and has invertible finite dihedral integers 2m_st. For n≤1 the Coxeter system has no colors.
items.proof_strategy: Use β_i=x_i−x_{i+1} for the positive-root length criterion and α_i=ε_iβ_i with alternating ε_i for the balanced Elias–Williamson realization. Verify the reflection action and graph convention, ∂_i(α_i h)=2h and surjectivity via δ_i=α_i/2, faithfulness and reflection faithfulness, balance [m_st−1]=1, and invertibility of 2m_st over Q.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: type a reduced words and the Coxeter presentation
items.statement: Any two reduced adjacent-transposition words for one permutation are connected by type-A braid moves. The abstract group on involutions t_i with far commutation and adjacent braid relations maps isomorphically to S_n under t_i↦(i i+1); n≤1 is trivial.
items.proof_strategy: Use the earlier Garside type-A lemma for inversion length and braid connectivity without citing the pending published Coxeter proof. Von Dyck gives a surjection from the abstract presentation. Induct on an arbitrary presentation-word length: append t_i to a reduced representative for τ; if inversions rise it remains reduced, and if they fall choose reduced r for τs_i, braid-connect the old representative to r t_i, and cancel t_i². Thus every kernel word reduces to the empty word, proving injectivity and the Coxeter presentation.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §3, PDF pp.11–13

items.title: type a Hecke algebra in Soergel normalization
items.statement: Let A=Z[v,v^{-1}], q=v^{-2}, and H_n be the unital A-algebra on T_1,…,T_(n−1) with Coxeter braid and distant-commutation relations and (T_i−q)(T_i+1)=0. Put H_i=v(T_i+1). Thus H_i^2=(v+v^{-1})H_i; for n≤1 let H_n=A.
items.proof_strategy: Define H_n by the displayed quotient of the free associative A-algebra. Expand T_i^2=(q−1)T_i+q and calculate H_i^2=v^2(T_i+1)^2=(v+v^{-1})H_i. Record the inverse change of generators T_i=v^{-1}H_i−1, exactly matching Elias–Williamson §2.1 and the final Soergel character convention. This is an internal presentation for BG-16; it asserts no finite-field specialization or Tits-deformation theorem.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §3.1, PDF pp.12–13

items.title: type a Hecke standard basis for Soergel comparison
items.statement: For w in S_n, let T_w be the product of the T_i along any reduced expression. Then {T_w:w in S_n} is an A-basis of H_n, and T_w T_i=T_(ws_i) for an ascent and (q−1)T_w+qT_(ws_i) for a descent. Equivalently the products of normalized H_i along reduced words form a triangular A-basis.
items.proof_strategy: The preceding braid-connectivity lemma makes T_w well-defined. For a descent write w=u s_i with reduced length and apply the quadratic relation; for an ascent append s_i. Induction on word length gives spanning. To prove independence, form E=⊕_(w∈S_n) A e_w and define right operators ρ_i by e_wρ_i=e_(ws_i) on ascents and e_wρ_i=(q−1)e_w+q e_(ws_i) on descents. Quadratic is immediate. For each pair i,j, split S_n into right cosets of the rank-two parabolic W_{ij}; a unique minimum-length representative makes the restriction of ρ_i,ρ_j the universal 4-state commuting case or 6-state adjacent case. Check these finite matrices satisfy ρ_iρ_j=ρ_jρ_i or ρ_iρ_jρ_i=ρ_jρ_iρ_j, respectively. Thus H_n acts on E, and e_e T_w=e_w; the T_w are independent. Finally H_i=vT_i+v has leading term vT_i, so reduced-word H-products are triangular with unit Laurent diagonal relative to T_w.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, Lemma 3.1, PDF p.13

items.title: type a soergel bimodule for a simple reflection
items.statement: For 1≤i<n define B_i=R⊗_{R^{s_i}}R(1), with EW shift M(1)_d=M_{d+1}=M{−1}_d in the library convention. Both outer R actions and total internal grading are specified.
items.proof_strategy: Define $B_i=R\otimes_{R^{s_i}}R(1)$ as a graded $(R,R)$-bimodule, where EW's $M(1)_d=M_{d+1}$ equals the library shift $M\{-1\}$. Keep this dictionary in every later formula.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: type a soergel generators are finite free on both sides
items.statement: Each B_i is graded free of rank two separately as a left and as a right R-module; every Bott–Samelson tensor product is finite free on both sides.
items.proof_strategy: Write $R=R^{s_i}\oplus\alpha_iR^{s_i}$ using $2^{-1}$ and the Demazure operator. Tensoring shows $B_i$ is graded free of rank two as a left $R$-module and separately as a right $R$-module, with the displayed shifts. Tensor products of the $B_i$ therefore retain finite projectivity on both sides.

items.title: bott samelson bimodule of a word
items.statement: For a word (i_1,…,i_r), define B_underlined-i=B_{i_1}⊗_R⋯⊗_R B_{i_r}, with the empty word giving R. Retain the expression in the notation: reduced words for the same permutation can give nonisomorphic Bott–Samelson bimodules.
items.proof_strategy: Form the balanced tensor product with its outer actions and total grading, using the finite-freeness supplier. The definition does not identify different reduced words; a later distinguished indecomposable summand is word-independent.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: the type a soergel category
items.statement: SBim_n is the idempotent-complete additive graded monoidal category of finite sums, internal shifts and direct summands of Bott–Samelson R-bimodules. Distinguish SBim_n from the later diagrammatic presentation D.
items.proof_strategy: Take the additive, graded-shift, idempotent-complete monoidal subcategory generated by the $B_i$; distinguish it from its diagrammatic presentation.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: type a standard graph bimodules support filtrations and character
items.statement: For w∈S_n, R_w is R on the left and has right action r·f=r w(f). Define graph support Γ_A M for subsets A⊆S_n, with separate Bruhat-principal y cutoffs and integer length cutoffs. Set Δ_w=R_w(−ℓ(w)), ∇_w=R_w(ℓ(w)); define length support flags, their multiplicities, and the two character sums, whose intrinsicness is proved later.
items.proof_strategy: Define graph supports scheme-theoretically by ideal-power annihilation. Keep Γ_{≤y},Γ_{≥y} as Bruhat-principal cutoffs and Γ_{≤i},Γ_{≥i} as length cutoffs for the flags. Define R_w, Δ_w(d), ∇_w(d) with the external/internal shift dictionary and give the Hecke standard-basis character weights; import the precise Soergel support-layer results used later.

items.title: Type-A graph-bimodule extension vanishing
items.statement: For distinct x,y in S_n whose graph intersection has codimension at least two in either graph, every graded short exact sequence 0→R_y(b)→E→R_x(a)→0 splits. If y=xt for a reflection t, localizing at the hyperplane equation α_t makes every such extension split.
items.proof_strategy: Choose a homogeneous lift e of 1 in R_x and let the graph-ideal generators ℓ_i act by ℓ_i e=m_i in R_y. Compatibility gives ℓ_i m_j=ℓ_j m_i. On R_y, row-reduce the linear forms ℓ_i to independent variables u_1,…,u_r followed by zeros, where r=codim(Gr(x)∩Gr(y)); r=1 exactly when x^{-1}y is a transposition. For r≥2, u_1m_2=u_2m_1 and coprimality of u_1,u_2 imply m_i=u_i m for one polynomial m; the zero-form equations force the remaining m_i=0. Replace e by e−m to split the sequence. For r=1, the only obstruction is a residue modulo u_1, killed on inverting u_1=α_t up to a unit. This is a self-contained type-A specialization of Soergel Lemma 5.8, with all linear polynomial facts proved in the step.

items.title: bott samelson bimodules have delta and nabla support filtrations
items.statement: Every Bott–Samelson bimodule has a Δ flag refining decreasing length support and a ∇ flag refining increasing length support, with graph subquotients indexed by subexpressions and shifts determined by the rank-one exact sequences.
items.proof_strategy: Use both rank-one exact sequences and Soergel Propositions 5.7 and 5.9 for the shifted left reflection functor B_s⊗_R−. Sidewise freeness gives exactness; opposites preserve each flag category and transfer left closure to right tensoring. Track the one-letter shifts and then induct on the word.

items.title: type a support filtration multiplicities are intrinsic
items.statement: The graded multiplicities of Δ_w(d) and ∇_w(d) in the corresponding support filtrations are independent of the compatible enumeration and are additive under direct sums and direct summands.
items.proof_strategy: Refine a Bruhat-compatible enumeration one adjacent incomparable pair at a time. The extension-vanishing lemma makes the two corresponding graph layers exchange without changing either isomorphism type or shift multiplicity. Hence the $\Delta_w(d)$ and $\nabla_w(d)$ multiplicities depend only on $M$, defining $h_\Delta(M)$ and $h_\nabla(M)$.

items.title: Frobenius biadjunction for type-A Soergel generators
items.statement: For each simple s, the graded Frobenius trace ∂_s:R→R^s induces left and right adjunctions making tensor with B_s self-biadjoint with the stated shift convention; give the unit and counit maps from dual bases.
items.proof_strategy: Use R=R^s⊕δR^s with δ=α_s/2 and ∂_s(f)=(f−s(f))/α_s. The trace pairing has dual bases {1,δ} and {−sδ,1}. Write the coevaluation from the dual-basis tensor and evaluation from ∂_s, check both triangle identities on 1 and δ, then translate the graded shift: B_s is self-adjoint in the EW (1) convention.

items.title: type a character recursion under simple Soergel tensoring
items.statement: For a Δ-flagged or ∇-flagged type-A bimodule M and simple reflection s_i, B_i⊗_R M has a corresponding support flag. Its character satisfies h_Δ(B_i M)=H_i h_Δ(M) and h_∇(B_i M)=H_i h_∇(M), where H_i=v(T_i+1); a grading shift (1) multiplies h_Δ by v and h_∇ by v^{-1}.
items.proof_strategy: Follow Soergel Propositions 5.7 and 5.9. In each pair of support strata x,s_i x, restrict a filtered M to R^{s_i} and use graph-extension vanishing to split exactly the extensions needed after restriction. Reinduce with R⊗_(R^{s_i})− and the two rank-one exact sequences. For the Δ flag this gives the two explicit multiplicity equations on Soergel PDF pp.14–15, which match left multiplication by H_i in the local Hecke standard basis. Apply the graded right-dual construction to obtain the ∇ equations and its v↦v^{-1} shift convention. Check the empty word unit. This asserts generator action only; arbitrary tensor-product multiplicativity is proved later after categorification.

references.title: Soergel, Kazhdan–Lusztig-Polynome und unzerlegbare Bimoduln, Propositions 5.7 and 5.9, PDF pp.13–16
Elias–Williamson, Soergel Calculus, §§2.1, 3.4, PDF pp.14 and 25–27

items.title: Special Bott–Samelson Hom formula before reflection localization
items.statement: For M with a Δ flag and N Bott–Samelson, or M Bott–Samelson and N with a ∇ flag, Hom_{R-R}(M,N) is graded free over R with rank Σ_{w,d,e}(M:Δ_w(d))(N:∇_w(e))v^{d−e} in the library generator-degree convention. This restricted formula precedes reflection localization.
items.proof_strategy: Prove the first case of Soergel Theorem 5.15 by peeling the leftmost B_s factor of the target, moving it across Hom via left biadjunction, applying the left character recursion and Hecke self-adjointness, and ending with the identity graph layer of Hom(M,R). Import the theorem’s dual case for Bott–Samelson sources; opposites do not exchange Δ and ∇. The library graded rank v^{degree} is the bar transform of Soergel’s rank convention.

items.title: type a top support layers are controlled by reflection localization
items.statement: For y∈S_n and M Bott–Samelson or a direct summand, fix c_t=x_a−x_b for each reflection t=(a b), a<b, and p_y=∏_{yt<y}c_t. For Bruhat-principal cutoffs, the natural maps identify Γ_yM with (underline Γ_{≤y}M)p_y and underline Γ_{≥y}M with (Γ^yM)p_y, yielding the graded-rank formulas.
items.proof_strategy: Use Soergel Satz 6.6 and its Lemma 6.10 localization argument with fixed positive coordinate hyperplane equations c_t. Keep the natural maps between the correct Bruhat y-layer subquotients, compute their p_y-divisible images and degrees, and extend the identities to direct summands by idempotents. The later full Hom formula is not used.

items.title: the type a soergel hom formula
items.statement: For M,N∈SBim_n, Hom_{R-R}(M,N) is graded free over R with graded rank Σ_{w,d,e}(M:Δ_w(d))(N:∇_w(e))v^{d−e}, equal to the standard pairing of their characters in the declared convention.
items.proof_strategy: Use the already proved special case and top-layer identities, then invoke Soergel Lemma 6.13 for arbitrary direct summands. Check its exact category and shift hypotheses against the local Soergel category and the generator-degree rank convention; identify the displayed sum with the Hecke pairing. Do not assume layerwise Hom surjectivity without the lemma.

items.title: the rank one soergel bimodule square splits
items.statement: For each simple i, B_i⊗_R B_i≅B_i(1)⊕B_i(−1) as graded R-bimodules.
items.proof_strategy: Since $2$ is invertible, $R=R^{s_i}\oplus\alpha_iR^{s_i}$; tensor this decomposition and write the multiplication/Demazure inclusions and projections proving $B_i\otimes_RB_i\cong B_i(1)\oplus B_i(-1)$.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: distant soergel generators commute
items.statement: If |i−j|>1, B_i⊗_R B_j≅B_j⊗_R B_i as graded R-bimodules.
items.proof_strategy: Identify invariant extensions for disjoint adjacent transpositions and write the bimodule isomorphism $B_iB_j\cong B_jB_i$.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: the rank two longest type a soergel bimodule
items.statement: For adjacent i,i+1 put B_{i,i+1,i}=R⊗_{R^{⟨s_i,s_{i+1}⟩}}R(3). It is the S_3 longest summand, equal to the Khovanov normalization R⊗_{R^{S_3}}R{−3}.
items.proof_strategy: For adjacent $s_i,s_{i+1}$ define $B_{i,i+1,i}=R\otimes_{R^{\langle s_i,s_{i+1}\rangle}}R(3)$. This is the longest $S_3$ summand in EW shifts, equivalent to Khovanov's $R\otimes_{R^{S_3}}R\{-3\}$.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: rank two type a soergel bimodule decompositions
items.statement: For adjacent i,i+1, B_iB_{i+1}B_i≅B_{i,i+1,i}⊕B_i and B_{i+1}B_iB_{i+1}≅B_{i,i+1,i}⊕B_{i+1}, with no additional grading shift.
items.proof_strategy: Construct the type-$A_2$ inclusion/projection maps from multiplication and divided differences and verify the two matrix composites, giving $B_iB_{i+1}B_i\cong B_{i,i+1,i}\oplus B_i$ and $B_{i+1}B_iB_{i+1}\cong B_{i,i+1,i}\oplus B_{i+1}$ with no extra shift.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: type a diagrammatic soergel category and its bimodule functor
items.statement: Define the Q-linear graded monoidal type-A diagram category D with polynomial boxes, dots, trivalent, distant four-valent and adjacent six-valent vertices modulo all Elias–Williamson relations, including the A_1×I_2(m), all-distant and A_3 three-colour families. Give the balanced-root generator normalization and the source-fixed 2m-valent maps as a candidate bimodule functor.
items.proof_strategy: Use Elias–Williamson Definitions 5.1, 5.2 and 5.12 with Elias–Khovanov type-A relations. Distinguish the half-scaled balanced unit dot Δ_s from the coordinate-root rank-two splitting element Z_s; use Libedinsky’s fixed 2m-valent maps, whose scalar is not set merely by existence of a common summand. Record the light/double-leaf and character source theorems accurately, with reduced-word objects distinct from their distinguished indecomposable summands.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5
Elias–Khovanov, Diagrammatics for Soergel Categories, §§3.4 and 5.1

items.title: split Grothendieck rings of type a Soergel categories
items.statement: For each essentially small graded additive monoidal category C=Kar(D) or SBim_n, choose a small skeleton and define K_0^split(C) as the free abelian group on object isomorphism classes modulo [X⊕Y]=[X]+[Y]. Tensor product gives [X][Y]=[X⊗Y] and the unit [1]; in the Soergel grading convention v[X]=[X(1)]=[X{−1}].
items.proof_strategy: The chosen skeleton prevents a proper-class free group. Bifunctorial additivity of tensor product makes multiplication independent of representatives and compatible with direct-sum relations; monoidal associativity and unit give a unital ring. The grading shift is an invertible additive autoequivalence compatible with tensor by natural identifications (X(1))⊗Y≅(X⊗Y)(1)≅X⊗(Y(1)), so v and v^{-1} act inversely and centrally. Explicitly reconcile EW M(1)_d=M_(d+1) with the library M{r}_d=M_(d−r), giving EW (1)=library {−1}. This local definition supplies only the split rings needed for the two BG-16 categories; it does not replace HA-19 general Grothendieck and Cartan theory.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, Definition 3, PDF pp.27–28

items.title: the type a diagrammatic relations hold for soergel bimodules
items.statement: Every defining type-A diagram relation is respected by the source-normalized bimodule maps, including the A_1×I_2(m), all-distant and A_3 three-colour families, so the generator assignment descends to a graded monoidal functor D→BSBim.
items.proof_strategy: Apply Elias–Williamson Claim 5.13 to the exact maps of Definition 5.12, including Libedinsky’s fixed 2m-valent generator, after checking the type-A realization hypotheses. Explain the polynomial, one-colour and distant relations and import the dihedral and rank-three relation checks for all three type-A families. The local rank-two decomposition verifies the common summand but is not itself a scalar normalization of the six-valent map.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5
Elias–Khovanov, Diagrammatics for Soergel Categories, §§3.4 and 5.1

items.title: double leaves form graded r bases of type a diagrammatic hom spaces
items.statement: For any two Bott–Samelson words, recursively constructed double leaves form a homogeneous free left R-basis of the Hom space in D, indexed by matching subexpressions with degrees given by their defects. When the target word is empty, the identity-product subfamily gives the light-leaf basis of Hom from the source word to the unit.
items.proof_strategy: Construct four local light-leaf maps U0,U1,D0,D1 for every subexpression, with degree equal to its defect, then glue pairs through a common reduced word. Over the fraction field, order graph summands by subexpressions: the localization matrix is triangular with nonzero diagonal, proving independence. For spanning, reproduce EW §7: negative–positive factorization, lower-term ideals I_w, Proposition 7.6 by the coupled maxwidth induction (L_M)/(X_M), and induction down Bruhat order. Thus every diagram reduces to double leaves; do not infer spanning from rank alone.

references.title: Libedinsky, Sur la catégorie des bimodules de Soergel, §§3–5

items.title: indecomposable type a diagrammatic soergel objects are indexed by permutations and shifts
items.statement: Over Q, Kar(D) is Krull–Schmidt and its indecomposables, up to isomorphism, are exactly the grading shifts D_w(d), one D_w for each w∈S_n.
items.proof_strategy: Use the double-leaves finite graded Hom basis to show finite-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism quotients, then Krull–Schmidt over the complete local field Q. In each reduced expression for w, localize to the unique top graph summand Q_w to isolate one primitive idempotent not factoring through lower Bruhat words. EW Theorem 6.25 uses the Jacobson radical argument to show every indecomposable has such a top index and is a shift of the associated D_w; the double-leaves lower-term quotient proves reduced-word independence.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: the diagrammatic character is the split k zero hecke isomorphism
items.statement: The diagrammatic character is an isomorphism of Z[v,v^{-1}]-algebras K_0^split(Kar(D))≅H_{S_n}, sending [D_i] to H_i and the distinguished indecomposable classes [D_w] to a basis triangular with unit diagonal over {tilde T_w}.
items.proof_strategy: Use Elias–Williamson (6.3) for the character of each Bott–Samelson word H_underlined-x and (6.4) for multiplication on word classes. Theorem 6.25 makes D_w a distinguished summand of a reduced-word object, not generally that whole object; Corollary 6.26 gives ch(D_w)=tilde T_w plus lower Bruhat terms. Transport this triangular basis to the library’s split K_0 presentation.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: light leaf maps form bases of type a soergel homs to the unit
items.statement: For every Bott–Samelson word, the evaluated recursive light leaves ending at the identity form a homogeneous free R-basis of Hom_{R-R}(B_word,R).
items.proof_strategy: Apply Libedinsky Theorem 5.1 recursively, using the same U0/U1/D0/D1 last-letter maps. Check degree defects and use the special/full Hom formula to count the target Hilbert series. Localize at reflection hyperplanes and order by maximal normal part to obtain an injective triangular coefficient matrix with unit diagonal. Equal graded ranks and Hom freeness then prove the chosen maps span over R.

references.title: Libedinsky, Sur la catégorie des bimodules de Soergel, §§3–5

items.title: evaluated double leaves form bases of type a soergel bimodule homs
items.statement: For every pair of Bott–Samelson words, the evaluated double leaves form a homogeneous free R-basis of their bimodule Hom space, with the same indexing and degrees as the diagrammatic double leaves.
items.proof_strategy: Evaluation is an isomorphism on unit-target Hom spaces because it sends the diagrammatic light-leaf basis to the evaluated basis. Right bending with the Frobenius cup and cap identifies Hom(x,y) with Hom(x rev(y),unit), preserves degrees and left R action, and commutes with evaluation. Thus evaluation is an isomorphism on arbitrary word Hom spaces and sends the diagrammatic double-leaf basis to a basis. No entrywise identification with bent light leaves or later equivalence theorem is used.

references.title: Libedinsky, Sur la catégorie des bimodules de Soergel, §§3–5

items.title: type a diagrammatic and bimodule soergel categories are equivalent
items.statement: The evaluation functor Kar(D)→SBim_n is an equivalence of graded monoidal categories for the standard type-A realization over Q.
items.proof_strategy: The functor sends each diagrammatic double leaf to the corresponding evaluated double leaf, which is a basis on every Bott–Samelson Hom; it is fully faithful. It is essentially surjective onto BSBim by construction. Extend across finite sums, shifts and idempotent completion. Explicitly use the verified standard type-A Soergel-realization hypotheses.

references.title: Libedinsky, Sur la catégorie des bimodules de Soergel, §§3–5

items.title: split grothendieck group of the soergel category is the type a hecke algebra
items.statement: There is an isomorphism K_0^split(SBim_n)≅H_{S_n} over Z[v,v^{-1}] with [B_i]↦H_i=v(T_i+1), q=v^{-2}, and T_i=v^{-1}H_i−1 under the declared RG-13 normalization. In particular [B_i]^2=(v+v^{-1})[B_i].
items.proof_strategy: Transport the diagrammatic character isomorphism across the proved monoidal equivalence, using the local split-K0 ring definition. Under the local Hecke presentation q=v^{-2}, set H_i=v(T_i+1), so T_i=v^{-1}H_i−1 and [B_i] corresponds to H_i. Directly compare the rank-one splitting [B_i]^2=(v+v^{-1})[B_i] with the expanded quadratic relation. This gives the full split-K0 isomorphism because the diagrammatic character is already an isomorphism.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §§2–5

items.title: the type a standard character is multiplicative
items.statement: On K_0^split(SBim_n), the intrinsic Δ- and ∇-multiplicity characters are multiplicative maps to the type-A Hecke algebra. The Δ-character is A-linear and sends the EW grading shift (1) to multiplication by v; the ∇-character sends that shift to multiplication by v^{-1}. For Bott–Samelson words, both obey the simple-generator subexpression recursion with EW shifts.
items.proof_strategy: Use the proved categorification isomorphism E:H_n→K_0^split(SBim_n). The earlier simple-tensor recursion and unit calculation show h_Δ∘E is the identity on all products of H_i, hence on H_n. Since E is surjective, h_Δ=E^{-1} and therefore h_Δ is multiplicative on arbitrary Soergel summands, including tensors of two summands. For h_∇ define the semilinear Hecke bar map d by d(v)=v^{-1} and d(T_i)=T_i^{-1}=q^{-1}T_i+(q^{-1}−1). The quadratic and braid relations make d a well-defined algebra involution; direct substitution gives d(H_i)=H_i. Soergel Proposition 5.9 identifies the right-dual ∇ character with d∘h_Δ on Bott–Samelson generators, while reversing the v-action on shifts. Bott–Samelson classes span K_0^split(SBim_n) by triangularity against the indecomposable basis, so equality extends to every summand. As d is a semilinear algebra involution fixing H_i, h_∇ is multiplicative, with the stated grading behavior. Do not infer this general result merely from tensoring two graph layers: Δ_s⊗Δ_s alone does not have the Hecke quadratic product.

title: Type-A Soergel Bimodules and Hecke Categorification — Examples

items.title: the rank one soergel category
items.statement: For n=2, compute R^s, the homogeneous basis 1,α, the two rank-one exact sequences, and explicit splitting maps for B_s^2≅B_s(1)⊕B_s(−1).
items.proof_strategy: Compute $R^s$, the homogeneous basis $1,\alpha$, and all splitting maps; EW rank-one calculus.

references.title: Libedinsky, Gentle Introduction to Soergel Bimodules I, §4

items.title: the type a two rank two soergel decomposition
items.statement: For n=3, compute the coordinate-root rank-two multiplication, insertion and Demazure maps and the degree-zero idempotent they form; verify B_1B_2B_1≅B_{121}⊕B_1 and B_2B_1B_2≅B_{121}⊕B_2 with matching graded ranks.
items.proof_strategy: Work in coordinate roots β_s=x_1−x_2, β_t=x_2−x_3. Check ∂_s(β_t)=−1, the four map degrees +1,+1,−1,−1 and the zig-zag factor ½·2. The idempotent gives the small summand and the rank-two theorem identifies its complement. Keep the balanced diagrammatic six-valent generator distinct from these coordinate maps.

items.title: hecke quadratic relation from the soergel square
items.statement: Taking split classes of B_i^2≅B_i(1)⊕B_i(−1) yields H_i^2=(v+v^{-1})H_i and, after H_i=v(T_i+1), the RG-13 quadratic relation (T_i−v^{-2})(T_i+1)=0.
items.proof_strategy: Take graded split classes and translate to RG-13's $T_i$; EW §1.

items.title: bott samelson words related by a braid need not be isomorphic bimodules
items.statement: For adjacent i,i+1, the two triple Bott–Samelson words related by the Coxeter braid have decompositions with common longest summand and distinct extra B_i versus B_{i+1}; their intrinsic graph multiplicities distinguish the words.
items.proof_strategy: Use the two rank-two decompositions. If the triple products were isomorphic, additivity and intrinsic uniqueness of graph filtration multiplicities would force the characters of B_i and B_{i+1} to coincide after cancelling the common longest term. But the R_{s_i} graph layer occurs in B_i and not B_{i+1}; calculate this from the rank-one exact sequence. The result concerns bimodules; later Rouquier complexes give the braid action.
